_meta.theme: work integrity: Merged must mean the work is in the base, and no paid-for work is ever destroyed
waves: r13-auto-recover (needs both: the archives must exist for every failure and the reuse path reuses the integrity helpers)
_meta.origin: All three are defects found by PROBING the current build, not by its own green tests: a non-committing agent produced 'done/merged' with nothing in the base (reproduced), and execute.rs cleanup() destroys the worktree AND branch on the agent-failure and heal paths.

tasks.title: Never report an attempt as merged unless its work actually landed: commit a dirty worktree before judging it, and fail an attempt that produced no change (an_attempt_that_produces_no_change_never_reports_merged, a_dirty_worktree_is_committed_before_the_attempt_is_judged)
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn an_attempt_that_produces_no_change_never_reports_merged' tests/e2e.rs && grep -q 'fn a_dirty_worktree_is_committed_before_the_attempt_is_judged' tests/e2e.rs && openspec validate --specs && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL: make `Merged` mean "the work is in the base". Today it does not, and this is the most serious defect found in this project so far: it is a FALSE GREEN — the tool reports success for a task whose work never landed.

REPRODUCTION (verified against the current build, with a non-committing agent and `accept: "test -f TOUCHED.txt"`): the agent writes `TOUCHED.txt`, exits 0, and never commits. Then
  - `changed_paths` (`git diff <base>...HEAD`) sees NOTHING, because the edit is uncommitted, so the scope check passes vacuously;
  - the acceptance gate RUNS IN THE WORKTREE, sees the dirty file, and PASSES;
  - `worktree::merge` runs `git merge --no-ff <branch>`, and because the branch tip IS the base, git answers "Already up to date" and exits 0;
  - `worktree::merge` therefore returns `Ok`, `execute_attempt` returns `Outcome::Merged`, the task is recorded `Done`, the worktree is removed with `cleanup` — and the agent's work is DESTROYED.
Observed output: `✓ dirty done (attempt 1)`, receipt outcome `merged`, no error, base branch containing only the initial commit. The gate never lied; the REPORTING did.

The same root cause is a SCOPE-ENFORCEMENT BYPASS: an agent can leave an out-of-scope edit uncommitted and `changed_paths` will not see it either, while the gate happily runs with that file present.

FIX, in `execute_attempt` (`src/execute.rs`), on the path where the agent exited 0 (after the `!agent_out.passed()` failure arm, BEFORE the scope-enforcement block):
1. DURABLE FIRST. If the worktree is dirty (`git status --porcelain` non-empty), stage and commit it on the attempt branch with a harness message like `af: <task-id> attempt <n> — agent left uncommitted work`. This must happen BEFORE the scope check, so that the scope check, the gate and the merge all judge EXACTLY the same content — the committed tree — instead of the gate judging the worktree while the merge carries nothing. If the commit fails, FAIL the attempt with a clear reason (`cannot commit the agent's uncommitted work: <stderr>`) instead of continuing; never proceed to the gate on a tree you could not make durable. Do not pass `--no-verify`: the operator's hooks are theirs.
2. NO CHANGE IS NOT SUCCESS. Immediately after, count the commits the branch has beyond the base with the EXISTING helper `worktree::commits_ahead(repo, base_branch, &wt.branch)` (`src/worktree.rs`). If the count is 0 the attempt produced nothing, so it MUST NOT be reported as merged and the task MUST NOT reach `Done`: append a log line naming the fact, `cleanup`, and return `Outcome::Failed` with a deterministic reason such as `agent produced no change: 0 commits ahead of <base> after <secs>s`. Rationale: `Merged` is the harness's claim that the base now contains the agent's work; with zero commits there is nothing to contain. A task that genuinely needs no change is a `manual: true` task (operator sign-off), and the "work was already merged by an earlier attempt whose Done was lost" case is handled BEFORE a fresh agent attempt by the resume machinery (`resume_merge_only`/`finish_resume_merge`), so it never reaches this guard.
3. BELT AND BRACES. Only return `Outcome::Merged` if the base really contains the branch afterwards: verify the branch tip is an ancestor of the base (the private `branch_merged_into_head` helper in `src/run.rs` does exactly this — reuse or mirror it; hoisting its visibility is fine). If the verification fails, return `Failed` naming the discrepancy rather than reporting a merge that did not happen.
4. Do not weaken anything existing: scope enforcement, the gate path, the round-11 archiving (scope violation / merge conflict), `gate_replay`, or the `Spend` carried on every post-agent failure.

TESTS (write them FIRST and confirm they fail for the right reason before implementing). The stub agent is `src/bin/example_agent.rs` and it currently ALWAYS commits its work (`git add -A && git commit -m "example_agent: task work"`, ignoring failures) — add an opt-in knob to it (for example `FAKE_AGENT_NO_COMMIT=1`) that skips the commit so the dirty-worktree case can be exercised, and keep the stub a THIN printer: put any real logic in a unit-tested pure function, because llvm-cov does not credit lines inside this spawned binary. Remember the stub's env knobs must ride `TF_AGENT_ENV_PASSTHROUGH` — the agent child's environment is otherwise stripped, and omitting it silently produces a test that measures nothing.
  - `an_attempt_that_produces_no_change_never_reports_merged` in `tests/e2e.rs`: a worker that produces no change at all must NOT reach `Done`, the receipt outcome must not be `merged`, and the reason must name the zero-commit condition.
  - `a_dirty_worktree_is_committed_before_the_attempt_is_judged` in `tests/e2e.rs`: with the no-commit knob on, a task whose gate requires the file the agent wrote must end `Done` WITH the change present in the base branch's committed tree (`git show base:<path>`) — proving the work landed instead of being destroyed — and the receipt must be honestly `merged` because a real merge happened.
  - If the full suite reveals an existing test that relies on a no-change attempt reaching `Done`, it is asserting this bug: fix the FIXTURE (make the stub produce a committed change) rather than weakening the guard, and report every such test in your final message.
5. SPEC: document the new contract in `openspec/specs/lifecycle/spec.md` (an attempt that produces no change is not merged; the attempt's work is made durable before it is judged) and, if the merge/commits contract lives there, `openspec/specs/worktree/spec.md`. Keep every surviving scenario verbatim (a modified requirement REPLACES the old block).
6. Run the repo's own CI checks before you stop (`openspec validate --specs`, `./scripts/coverage-gate.sh`, `cargo test`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`); the acceptance gate runs exactly those.

tasks.title: Keep the attempt's work on every failure path: archive it when the agent stalls, times out or exits non-zero, and when startup heal sweeps an interrupted attempt (a_stalled_attempt_keeps_its_work_under_an_archived_branch)
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn a_stalled_attempt_keeps_its_work_under_an_archived_branch' tests/e2e.rs && openspec validate --specs && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL: finish the guarantee round 11 started. Round 11 preserved the agent's committed work when a SCOPE VIOLATION or a MERGE CONFLICT failed an attempt. Two more paths still destroy it, and they are the ones where the most work is at stake.

PATH 1 — THE AGENT ITSELF FAILED. In `execute_attempt` (`src/execute.rs`), the `!agent_out.passed()` arm (the stall-watchdog kill, the total timeout, and any non-zero agent exit) calls `cleanup(&repo, &wt)`, which is `worktree::remove` = `git worktree remove --force` PLUS `git branch -D`. A worker that stalls after 60 minutes of editing and committing loses everything it did, and `agent_timeout_s`/`TF_AGENT_STALL_S` make that the single most expensive failure the harness has. Fix it exactly the way round 11 fixed the scope-violation arm: call `worktree::archive_branch(&repo, &wt.branch, now_ts())` BEFORE `cleanup`, append `-- work kept on branch <name>`, and append `; work kept on branch <name>` to the failure reason. Archiving is a courtesy and must never fail the attempt: when it yields `None` the message is unchanged. Only archive when the branch actually carries work — use `worktree::commits_ahead` to check, so a stall at minute zero does not create a meaningless archive ref.
  Also cover the two neighbouring arms in the same scope-check block that cleanup and lose the work today: the `worktree::current_branch` error arm and the `changed_paths` error arm (they currently `cleanup` and return `Failed(e)`). If a dirty worktree has to be preserved, commit it first the way the `r13-work-integrity` change does — that helper is your predecessor's; reuse it rather than writing a second one.

PATH 2 — THE ORCHESTRATOR WAS INTERRUPTED. `worktree::heal` (`src/worktree.rs`) runs at startup and removes the worktree (and branch) of every task that is not currently running — that is exactly the "af was killed mid-attempt" case, where the agent may have committed real work. It already receives the branch prefix and the task ids, so it can archive the branch before removing it, for the same reason and with the same best-effort rule. Keep the existing behaviour that running tasks are never touched, and keep `heal` non-fatal.

ALSO: the reused-gate-failure arm (a gate-only retry whose gate fails a second time) currently `cleanup`s and thereby destroys the very work the retry was built to preserve. Archive it there too.

TESTS (write them FIRST and confirm they fail for the right reason). Required: `a_stalled_attempt_keeps_its_work_under_an_archived_branch` in `tests/e2e.rs` — drive the stall watchdog (the stub honours `FAKE_AGENT_HANG_MS`, capped at 2000ms) with a worker that commits work and then hangs; after the run, the receipt must name the archived branch, the branch must exist, its tip must contain the work, and the task must NOT be `Done`. Add: a total-timeout arm, and a `tests/contract_worktree.rs` unit test proving `heal` archives before it removes (and still never touches a running task). Stub env knobs must ride `TF_AGENT_ENV_PASSTHROUGH` — the agent child's environment is stripped otherwise and the test silently measures nothing. Keep the stub a thin printer: llvm-cov does not credit lines inside that spawned binary.

SPEC: extend the worktree/lifecycle specs so the preservation guarantee reads as "on every failure path", and name the archive form. Keep every surviving scenario verbatim (a modified requirement REPLACES the old block).

Run the repo's own CI checks before you stop (`openspec validate --specs`, `./scripts/coverage-gate.sh`, `cargo test`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`); the acceptance gate runs exactly those.

tasks.title: Make `af run` reuse a scope-compatible archived branch instead of paying an agent again (a_run_reuses_a_scope_compatible_archived_branch_without_paying_an_agent)
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn a_run_reuses_a_scope_compatible_archived_branch_without_paying_an_agent' tests/e2e.rs && openspec validate --specs && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL: stop paying an agent for work the harness already owns.

Rounds 11 and 12 built the two halves: every failure path now ARCHIVES the attempt's branch as `<branch>-rejected-<ts>` (`worktree::archive_branch`), and `af recover --task ID` (round 12) re-validates such a branch against the task's CURRENT scope and gate and merges it without re-invoking the agent. But `af recover` is MANUAL, so the money is still lost in the normal workflow: the operator widens an over-narrow scope and re-runs `af run`, which dispatches a fresh agent and re-buys work it already has on disk. The measured cost of that mistake is 2200.7s (round 8), 1987.4s (round 10) and 1785.8s (round 11).

FIX: in the run loop (`src/run.rs`, at the point where a ready task's deps are met and a worker is about to be picked/dispatched), FIRST look for a reusable archived branch for that task in its repo:
  - find branches matching `<branch_prefix>/<id>-rejected-<ts>` (and the `-<ts>-<n>` collision form) and take the NEWEST by PARSING the timestamp — never git's ordering or committer dates (the round-12 parser in `src/worktree.rs` already does this; reuse it, do not write a second one);
  - check that its changed paths relative to the merge base all pass the task's CURRENT `scope` — reuse `execute::changed_paths` + `execute::scope_violations` so admission and enforcement agree (round 12 hoisted them to `pub(crate)`);
  - if one qualifies, run the acceptance gate on it (unless `manual`) in a worktree, exactly as `run::recover` does: gate passes -> merge it with the standard message `af: <id> — <title>`, mark the task `Done` with `phase = GatePassed`, delete the archived branch, print a line naming what happened (for example `↺ <id> reused archived branch <name> (scope allows it; gate re-run, agent not re-run)`), and take NO agent dispatch for it. Gate fails -> fall through to the normal agent dispatch (do not retry the archive again in this run) and leave the branch alone for `af clean`/a later `recover`.
  - Log WHY a candidate was rejected (out of scope / gate failed / none found) at most once per attempt so a long campaign log stays readable.
SAFETY AND CONSTRAINT: the gate remains the sole arbiter — nothing is merged that the current gate does not pass — so this can only ever save money, never accept work that a fresh attempt would have had to redo. Default ON (that is the point), with an explicit escape hatch for an operator who wants a clean re-run (`TF_NO_REUSE=1`, documented in the README-independent help/spec text you touch), and it must never fire for a task with no archive, a task whose archive is out of scope, or a task already `Done`. Reuse must not double-count a receipt: the attempt that produced the archived branch already has one, and the reuse itself is not a new attempt — if you need durable evidence of the reuse, follow round 12's precedent rather than inventing a second ledger.

TESTS: required `a_run_reuses_a_scope_compatible_archived_branch_without_paying_an_agent` in `tests/e2e.rs` — an end-to-end run where an archived branch already satisfies the task's gate and scope: assert the task reaches `Done`, the base contains the change, the archived branch is gone, and the agent was NEVER invoked (count invocations by counting the `-- agent --` marker in the attempt log, or by having the stub write a file each time it runs — the stub's writes are overwrites, so a marker line in the log is the reliable counter). Add the negative arms in `tests/cli.rs`: an out-of-scope archive falls through and dispatches the agent; a gate-failing archive falls through; `TF_NO_REUSE=1` never reuses. Stub env knobs must ride `TF_AGENT_ENV_PASSTHROUGH`.

SPEC: document the pre-dispatch reuse decision in `openspec/specs/lifecycle/spec.md` and the operator-visible behaviour in `openspec/specs/cli/spec.md`. Keep every surviving scenario verbatim (a modified requirement REPLACES the old block).

Run the repo's own CI checks before you stop (`openspec validate --specs`, `./scripts/coverage-gate.sh`, `cargo test`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`); the acceptance gate runs exactly those.
